newsitem.title: UK: New funding firm backs large European telecom deal.
newsitem.headline: New funding firm backs large European telecom deal.

text.p: Callahan Associates International (CAI), a new funding group led by U.S. telecom veteran Richard Callahan, said on Tuesday it was poised to announce a large European telecom project worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

"I can't tell you whether it will be a cellular or a cable deal or anything else -- but I can tell you that it will be a large project and it will be in Europe," Callahan told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said the deal would be announced this month when sponsoring investors and other backers would also be identified.

CAI, which plans to finance, develop and buy wireless, communications and entertainment projects worldwide, said it had substantial financial backing and expected several billion dollars worth of equity to be invested over the next five years.
CAI said it had already spotted more than 100 major telecoms projects for funding and developing over the next few years and expected to announce three projects this year.
Callahan, the former president of telecom group U S West Inc's U S West International unit, said most projects would be worth $60-$250 million.
But the group's first project, in which it will buy into an existing telecom system and expand it, is likely to be bigger, Callahan said.

Callahan said a new kind of development vehicle was needed for the information age as the number of telephone lines world-wide are expected to double by 2000 and nations upgrade their telecommunications and entertainment systems.

"What is needed is something that is lean enough to be fast and flexible and yet has the stature to access large amounts of capital and the management expertise to ensure that capital is wisely invested and professionally managed.
"That is why we have created CAI," he said in a statement.

The group, which will open offices in London, the U.S. cities of Denver, Colorado and Westport, Connecticut, and in Asia in its second year, said it would finance projects by drawing on a small number of core sponsoring investors.
Callahan has more than 34 years of experience in the U.S. telecom industry and 10 years of experience in the international arena.

He has brought together a senior executive team including asset manager and merchant banker William Gordon, former president of merchant bank Quoin Financial Corp, which is active in telecoms in South East Asia.

David Colley, managing director and chief operating officer of London's largest cable TV operator Videotron Groupe also joins the group, as does Jay Dehejia, an expert in Asian business development and operations.
